atc_4455.interpretation: Same adequacy with flexible hydro removes the small 9.03 MW BESS build in this focused case.

atc_3564.interpretation: Intraday hydro flexibility removes the flat-hydro shortage and avoids the otherwise cap-binding wind/BESS build in the focused sensitivity.

atc_2673.interpretation: Hydro timing materially lowers shortage, but hard transfer stress remains binding even with candidate limits.

interpretation: Flattening daily hydro energy across 24 hours materially overstates shortage in several 2030 proxy cases.
At full ATC and reference demand, daily-energy intraday hydro redispatch removes about 96.9% of the flat-hydro unserved energy while preserving the same daily hydro MWh.
At 80% ATC the flexibility benefit remains large, but at 60% ATC interstate-transfer scarcity dominates and substantial shortage remains.
A single 130 MW Idukki-unit outage has a smaller effect than the flat-versus-flexible hydro timing assumption; broad 20% derating becomes more visible in the hardest transfer cases.

Partial-cost comparisons are only directly comparable when served energy is unchanged. Where flexible hydro reduces unserved energy, higher import expenditure can reflect serving load that was previously shed.
limitations: Daily hydro MWh are observed/imputed FY2024-25 totals, not future inflow forecasts.
No inter-day reservoir energy state, storage-volume curve or seasonal water optimization.
No cascade routing, travel time, head-dependent efficiency or environmental/irrigation release constraints.
Major station capacity groups are explicit, but observed daily hydro energy is not allocated to individual stations.
The N-1 Idukki case is source-anchored; 90% and 80% availability cases are synthetic stress assumptions.
No observed forced-outage chronology or probabilistic reliability.
Not a validated capacity plan or total-system-cost result.
